content.text:
I'd call it a draw. If my gemel is in one of the big houses' equity tracks, I'm not losing real money by staying put. Fairly sure, but I still don't know exactly which line in the table is my fund.

**What decided it:** I sorted the table by the 5-year average return. The equity tracks of הראל, מגדל, מנורה, כלל, הפניקס, מיטב, אנליסט and אלפא מור all land between 12.06% and 12.65% a year. All of them charge about 0.5–0.6% on assets and close to 0% on deposits, so there's no fee story either. Only two ordinary tracks really stand out: מיטב גמל עוקב מדדי מניות at 17.19% and אינפיניטי מניות at 15.81%. Both also show the highest 1-year numbers on the table, so I'd want a longer history before moving accounts over that. The S&P 500 trackers are about 12% on the 5-year average but only about 7% over the last 12 months, which I'm guessing is the dollar against the shekel. The page doesn't say.

**How it went:**
- **The site:** it's the regulator's site (רשות שוק ההון), so nobody is paid and no broker is pushing anything. The design looks about 20 years old.
- **First tab ("קופות גמל"):** the "סינון ברשימה" filter did nothing when I typed "מניות", not even after Enter.
- **"תחקור לפי פרמטרים" tab:** this is where the useful part is. I picked fund type תגמולים and specialization "מניות", and got back two funds, both marked ** (closed sector funds). So that filter is basically useless: "כלל תמר מניות" and the other big equity tracks don't count as "מניות".
- **Without the specialization filter:** I got all the funds in one dense table: 1y, 3y average, 5y average, Sharpe ("שארפ"), fee on assets and on deposits. That's the table I wanted.
- **Sorting:** clicking the sort arrow on the 5-year column looks like it does nothing. The page jumps to the middle of the sorted list and the rows above look like they're still in fund-number order. I nearly gave up on it. Only after scrolling did I see it had actually sorted.
- **What I didn't open:** "הסברים", "מדדי סיכון", "מקורות המידע". I also ignored the pie charts at the bottom.

**Things that bugged me:**
- The 12-month return and the "cumulative for the report period" columns are identical at the default 12-month setting, so one of them is a wasted column.
- No way to type my fund name in the parameters tab and highlight it.
- The rows run about 8,400 px of scrolling.

I'd have closed the tab after the two-funds result if I hadn't tried removing the filter.
